newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Metal Manufactures sees lower first half.
newsitem.headline: Metal Manufactures sees lower first half.

text.p: Cable and building materials manufacturer Metal Manufacturs Ltd said on Wednesday it now expected lower results in its first half ending June 30.
"As we see little improvement in domestic market conditions, we now expect our results for the first half will be below those of last year," chairman Kevin Kirby told the company's annual meeting.
Kirby said intense price competiton in the group's domestic markets and lower demand for cable from Australia's two main telecommunications companies were the key factors.
"We have also observed an increase in the intensity of price competition in almost all our businesses," Kirby said.

Metal Manufactures, about 61.5 percent owned by BICC Plc , said there were some early signs of increased activity in the housing and construction sectors which should translate into higher demand for the company's products over coming months.
Metal Manufactures reported a lower net profit of A$38.5 million for calendar 1996, compared with A$46.85 million in 1995.
Metal Manufactures managing director Glenn Dudley said after the meeting that it was too early to project whether the full calendar year profit would be above or below the previous year.
He said the current talks between Optus and Telstra on joint optic fibre cable networks would, if successful, obviously further reduce demand for the cables the company produces.
He also said the company's full year profit performance would depend on a significant upturn in the housing industry.
He said he did not see any major signs of such an upturn at the present time.
